title: KatalIArc seed catalog of architectural tactics

source.citation: Bass, Clements, and Kazman (2021), Software Architecture in Practice, 4th edition.
source.verification_status: bibliographic source identified; tactic-to-page mapping requires local verification
source.use: Candidate generation only; the catalog is not evidence that a tactic fits or will satisfy a scenario.

tactics.name: Reduce resource demand
tactics.mechanism: Reduce the amount or frequency of work required to produce a response, for example by filtering, aggregating, or reducing repeated computation.
conditions: A demand source or repeated work can be identified.
limitations: The actual bottleneck and workload are not established without measurements.

tactics.name: Manage resources
tactics.mechanism: Allocate, schedule, or coordinate constrained resources so competing work uses them effectively.
conditions: The relevant resource and contention mechanism are known.
limitations: Scheduling or pooling can add coordination overhead and does not create capacity.

tactics.name: Increase resources
tactics.mechanism: Add or increase processing, memory, network, or other capacity used by the response path.
conditions: The constrained resource and scaling boundary are identified.
limitations: Additional capacity may not help when the bottleneck is elsewhere; cost and coordination may rise.

tactics.name: Detect faults
tactics.mechanism: Detect a fault using mechanisms such as heartbeat, timeout, exception, or consistency checks.
conditions: Fault symptoms and detection thresholds can be defined.
limitations: Detection alone does not restore service and may produce false positives.

tactics.name: Recover from faults
tactics.mechanism: Restore service or state after a fault through recovery, reinitialization, rollback, or redundancy.
conditions: Recovery behavior, state ownership, and recovery objectives are understood.
limitations: Recovery can lose or duplicate work and depends on fault isolation and state consistency.

tactics.name: Prevent faults
tactics.mechanism: Reduce the probability that faults occur or propagate, using isolation, validation, or controlled removal from service.
conditions: Relevant fault sources and propagation paths are understood.
limitations: Prevention cannot eliminate all faults and may add operational complexity.

tactics.name: Localize changes
tactics.mechanism: Constrain the effects of a likely change to a small set of modules or components.
conditions: Change sources and the responsibilities they affect are understood.
limitations: Boundaries can add indirection and may not match future change patterns.

tactics.name: Prevent ripple effects
tactics.mechanism: Use stable interfaces, encapsulation, or dependency control to limit propagation of a change.
conditions: Coupling paths and interface ownership can be identified.
limitations: Abstraction can become costly or misleading when it does not correspond to real variation.

tactics.name: Defer binding time
tactics.mechanism: Move a choice to a later lifecycle stage so it can be changed with less redevelopment.
conditions: The decision can safely remain configurable or replaceable until that stage.
limitations: Late binding shifts complexity to configuration, deployment, or runtime validation.

tactics.name: Resist attacks
tactics.mechanism: Prevent unauthorized access or reduce attack opportunity through authentication, authorization, input validation, or isolation.
conditions: Assets, trust boundaries, and relevant threats are identified.
limitations: A control only addresses its stated threat model and can introduce usability or operational costs.

tactics.name: Detect attacks
tactics.mechanism: Recognize suspicious activity through monitoring, audit, or anomaly detection and raise an actionable signal.
conditions: Relevant events can be observed and an operational response exists.
limitations: Detection does not prevent impact and may miss or misclassify activity.

tactics.name: Recover from attacks
tactics.mechanism: Restore trusted service or data after a security incident using recovery, isolation, or rollback mechanisms.
conditions: Recovery points, trusted state, and incident responsibilities are defined.
limitations: Recovery cannot undo disclosure and depends on the integrity of backups and procedures.
